scenarios.title: Super-Agent {Al} Courts {J}
scenarios.text: Expensive watch, cheap cologne, a laminated folder of players he says he has “placed” in Europe and the Gulf. {A} slides a contract across the table: 10% of everything, exclusive, three years. “Sign with me and you won't be here in two years.”

choices.label: Sign now
choices.hint: Could open doors — or be a shark.

out.text: Six weeks in, {A}'s phone is always “in a meeting”. The small print says 15%, not 10%.
{A} is the real thing: three calls a day, every scout's number, a plan.

choices.label: Check his references
choices.desc: Call players he claims to represent.

out.text: Two of the “clients” have never heard of him. {J} deletes the number and finds a smaller, honest agent through a former coach.
The references check out. {J} signs, with a lawyer reading every line first.

choices.label: Stay as you are
choices.text: {J} says no thanks. {A} smiles like he's heard that before.

scenarios.title: A Top Agency Wants to Represent {J}
scenarios.text: One of the world's biggest football agencies sends a representative: glossy brochures, offices on three continents, clients you've seen on television. They want {J}. His current agent doesn't know yet.

choices.label: Switch
choices.hint: Your current agent will be hurt, maybe litigious.

out.text: The new agency moves fast: two sponsor calls in the first week. The old agent sends one bitter message.
The old agent's contract has a release fee nobody mentioned. Lawyers get involved.

choices.label: Stay loyal
choices.desc: He was there at the start.
choices.text: {J} stays with his agent. When the agent hears about the offer, he works twice as hard.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Agent Has a Side Deal
scenarios.text: {J} finds out his agent has been taking a secret fee from a club for steering him toward a transfer he didn't want. The email was forwarded by mistake.

choices.label: Fire him
choices.text: {J} fires him by phone. Then he spends two weeks finding someone honest. The new agent costs less and calls more.

choices.label: Confront him, stay
choices.hint: He'll be careful now. Or better at hiding.
choices.text: The agent apologises at length and cuts his fee. {J} doesn't fully trust him again.

scenarios.title: {J} Offered a Sponsorship Deal
text: A sportswear brand wants {J}'s face on billboards: {deal} a year, two years, four content days and a boot clause. His agent says it's fair. His agent also says it could be more.
A mobile phone brand wants {J} for a regional campaign: {deal} a year, two years. The advert involves him doing tricks with a phone instead of a ball.

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: {J} signs. A week later his face is ten metres tall on a billboard near his parents' house.

choices.label: Hold out for more
choices.hint: A better deal — or no deal.

ok.text: The brand comes back with 40% more. {J}'s agent is insufferable for days.

bad.text: The brand signs a teammate instead. His billboard goes up at the training-ground roundabout.

scenarios.title: {BRAND_boots} Want {J}
scenarios.text: {BRAND_boots} offer {J} a personalised boot deal: his own colourway, his name on the tongue, {deal} a year. The catch: three years exclusive, and his current boots are much more comfortable.

out.text: The first pair with his name on them arrives in a box like a jewel. He wears them to bed the first night.
The new boots give him blisters for a month. He plays through it; the money helps.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} keeps his old boots. His agent sighs dramatically.

scenarios.title: Friend Pitches {J} an Investment
text: A childhood friend with a new car and a pitch deck: a chain of coffee shops. “Guaranteed returns, bro. Everyone's in.” He wants {amount}.
A teammate's cousin is raising money for a crypto token “backed by footballers”. The website is very shiny. He wants {amount}.

choices.label: Invest
choices.text: {J} transfers the money. His friend sends a long voice note full of fire emojis.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: The friend stops replying to messages for a while.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Investment: The Verdict
scenarios.text: The investment {J} made months ago has finally reached a verdict.

out.text: Gone. All of it. So is the friend: his number is disconnected.
It limps along. {J} gets his money back and decides that's a win.
It actually works. The return lands: a healthy profit on what he put in.

scenarios.title: {J} Eyes a New Car
scenarios.text: Half the squad drives something that roars. {J} still drives the car his father helped him buy. The dealership has a matte black one for {price}, “special price for footballers”.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.hint: Big dent in savings. Instagram loves it.
choices.text: The car photo gets more likes than his last goal. His mother asks how much it cost and he lies.

choices.label: Keep the old one
choices.text: The old car survives another season. So do his savings.

scenarios.title: The Watch Everyone Has
scenarios.text: In the dressing room, watches are a language. The senior players all wear the same Swiss brand. A jeweller who “looks after footballers” has one for {J}: {price}.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.text: {J} wears it to training. Three teammates notice immediately. His bank balance notices too.

choices.label: No
choices.text: {J} declines. The jeweller leaves a card “for when you're ready”.

scenarios.title: Investment Property Opportunity
scenarios.text: A financial adviser recommended by the club suggests buying an apartment to rent out: steady income, a long-term asset. The price is {price}.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.text: {J} buys the apartment. The first rent payment arrives the next month. Boring, beautiful money.

choices.label: Keep cash
choices.text: {J} keeps his savings liquid.

scenarios.title: Tax Authority Sends {J} a Letter
scenarios.text: A letter from the tax office: an error in last year's declaration, an unpaid amount of {bill}, plus a fine if not paid in thirty days. His agent says the accountant made the mistake. The accountant says the agent did.

choices.label: Pay immediately
choices.text: {J} pays. He also hires a new accountant.

choices.label: Fight it with lawyers
choices.hint: Could save money — or become a headline.

out.text: The lawyers prove the mistake was the tax office's. Nothing to pay.
The case leaks to the press: “{J} in tax dispute.” He pays anyway, plus the lawyers.

scenarios.title: Teammates Gamble on the Team Bus
scenarios.text: Online casino apps are everywhere in the dressing room. A teammate shows {J} how much he won last night. It's more than {J} earns in a month.

out.text: {J} loses a small amount, feels sick, and deletes the app. Lesson learned cheaply.
{J} wins. Then bets again. Then loses more than he won. The app stays on his phone.

choices.label: Never
choices.text: {J} shakes his head. He's seen what it did to his uncle.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Gambling Is Getting Worse
scenarios.text: 3am, lying in bed, refreshing a betting app. {J} has lost {loss} this month. He's been chasing losses. He's started hiding his phone from his teammates.

choices.label: Tell the club, get help
choices.text: {J} tells the club doctor. A specialist, a self-exclusion order, weekly sessions. It's the hardest thing he's done. The app is gone.

out.text: He deletes it and it works. He doesn't miss it after a month.
He reinstalls it on day four.

scenarios.title: {J} Learns a Worse Player Earns More
scenarios.text: A teammate shows {J} his payslip by accident: a player who barely plays earns almost double what {J} does. {J} is the club's best player this season.

ok.text: The board reviews {J}'s contract and offers a raise. Not double, but meaningful.

bad.text: The board says contracts are contracts. {J} leaves the meeting with nothing but resentment.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: {J} lets it go. His agent writes it down for the next negotiation.

scenarios.title: Wages Are Late Again
scenarios.text: Payday comes and goes. The club says there's a “delay with the sponsor”. It's the second time this season. {J} has rent to pay and family expecting money.

out.text: The money arrives nine days late, without apology.
Only half arrives. The rest is promised “after the next home match”.

choices.label: Complain to the players' union
choices.text: The union steps in and the money arrives within a week, along with a frosty email from the club secretary.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Bank Account Is Nearly Empty
scenarios.text: {J} checks his banking app and feels sick. The car payment, the apartment, the restaurants, family transfers, all of it adds up to more than he earns. Payday is two weeks away.

choices.label: Cut everything back
choices.text: {J} moves to a smaller apartment and cooks for himself for the first time. He's surprisingly good at it.

choices.label: Hire a financial adviser
choices.text: The adviser builds a budget and takes {J}'s card for “safekeeping”. It works.

choices.label: Borrow from a teammate
choices.text: A teammate lends him money without asking questions. {J} pays it back on payday and never forgets the favour.

scenarios.title: A Charity Asks for a Donation
scenarios.text: A charity representative visits the training ground: an orphanage needs a new roof. Photos of smiling children, an official-looking document. They need {cost}.

out.text: The orphanage sends photos of the new roof and a drawing by the children. Real, and good.
There is no orphanage. The police say the same people visited three other clubs.

choices.label: Ask the club to verify it

out.text: The club verifies it. {J} donates and visits the orphanage himself.
The club finds it's a scam. {J} reports it. Three arrests.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Own Clothing Line?
scenarios.text: A designer friend proposes a streetwear brand with {J}'s initials and shirt number. Startup cost: {cost}. Fans would buy anything with his name on it. Probably.

choices.label: Launch it
choices.text: The launch post goes up. The first batch sells out in two days. The second batch is still in a warehouse.

choices.label: Not now
choices.text: {J} says maybe later.

scenarios.title: {J}'s Clothing Brand: One Year Later
scenarios.text: The accountant sends the annual numbers for the clothing brand.

out.text: Profit. Not huge, but real. A department store wants to stock it.
The brand loses money. {J} closes it and keeps one hoodie as a souvenir.

scenarios.title: A Sponsor Is Reconsidering
scenarios.text: {J}'s sponsor calls his agent: poor form, fewer minutes, less visibility. They're “reviewing the partnership”.

choices.label: Offer extra content days
choices.text: {J} offers four extra content days. The sponsor stays, happily.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.text: The sponsor leaves. {J} focuses on getting his form back.

scenarios.title: The Restaurant Bill Lands in Front of {J}
scenarios.text: Dinner with friends from home: twelve people, steaks, desserts, drinks. When the bill comes, everyone looks at {J}. It's {bill}.

choices.label: Pay for everyone
choices.text: {J} pays. Everyone cheers. Next time, they'll order more.

choices.label: Split it
choices.text: {J} suggests splitting. An awkward pause, then everyone pays. Two friends stop calling.

scenarios.title: Owner Pays a Surprise Win Bonus
scenarios.text: After a big win, the club owner bursts into the dressing room and announces a cash bonus for every player. {J}'s share: {bonus}.
scenarios.prompt: What do you do with the bonus?

choices.label: Send it home
choices.text: The whole bonus goes to his mother. She uses it to fix the kitchen.

choices.label: Save it
choices.text: Straight into savings.

choices.label: Treat yourself
choices.text: New headphones and a jacket he doesn't need. He loves both.

scenarios.title: Other Players Swear by an Investment Fund
scenarios.text: Three senior players have put money into a private fund that pays 8% a month. They show {J} their returns. The fund manager wants {amount} to “reserve his spot”.

out.text: Returns arrive for three months. Then the website goes down. The manager disappears. Forty footballers lose their savings.
{J} gets lucky and withdraws before the collapse. Others don't.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. Six months later, the fund collapses. His teammates lose everything.

scenarios.title: Indomie Want {J}
scenarios.text: Indomie want {J} in a TV advert: eating noodles after training, smiling. {deal} for a year. The nutritionist will not be pleased.

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: The advert plays during every match broadcast. Kids start copying his noodle-slurping face.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. A rival player takes the deal.

scenarios.title: Crypto Platform Wants {J} as Ambassador
scenarios.text: A crypto trading platform offers {fee} for {J} to become a “brand ambassador”: three posts a month telling fans to download the app.

choices.label: Take it
choices.hint: If it collapses, so does your name.

out.text: The money is real and the platform survives. For now.
The platform collapses eight months later. Fans who followed {J}'s posts lose money. Some blame him.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. His agent thinks he's mad. His fans will never know what he protected them from.

scenarios.title: Insure {J}'s Career?
scenarios.text: An insurance broker offers a career-ending-injury policy: {cost} a year, paying out a large sum if {J} can never play again. Most players never claim. Some wish they had insured.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.text: {J} signs. He hopes it's the worst money he ever spends.

choices.label: Skip it
choices.text: {J} skips it.

scenarios.title: Sponsor Event the Day Before a Match
scenarios.text: A club sponsor wants {J} at a shopping-mall event: two hours of signing, photos and a dance with the mascot. Fee: {fee}. It's the day before a match.

choices.label: Attend
choices.text: Three hundred fans, a dancing mascot, sore wrists from signing. {J} goes home exhausted and paid.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} declines. {M} quietly approves.

scenarios.title: Tenant Problems at {J}'s Apartment
scenarios.text: The tenant in {J}'s investment apartment has stopped paying rent and stopped answering the phone. The property manager wants instructions.

out.text: The tenant lost their job. They pay everything back over six months, with a thank-you letter.
The tenant leaves in the night with the furniture.

choices.label: Evict
choices.text: The eviction goes through. A new tenant moves in the next month.

scenarios.title: Free Gifts Keep Arriving
scenarios.text: Boxes arrive every day: shoes, headphones, skincare, energy drinks, gaming chairs. Brands want one post. Some send invoices afterwards, hoping he won't notice.
scenarios.prompt: What do you do with it all?

choices.label: Donate it
choices.desc: Give it to a youth club.
choices.text: A van of free gear goes to an orphanage football team. Their kit is now better than his club's.

choices.label: Keep it and post
choices.text: {J}'s apartment fills up with gear. Brands are happy. So is his little brother.

scenarios.title: Someone Claims {J}'s Family Owes Them Money
scenarios.text: A man arrives at the training ground claiming {J}'s father borrowed {cost} from him ten years ago. He has a handwritten note. His father says it's complicated.

choices.label: Pay it to end it
choices.text: {J} pays. His father won't look him in the eye for a week, then hugs him for a full minute.

out.text: The note is fake. The man disappears when the lawyer calls.
The debt is real. {J} pays it, with interest.

scenarios.title: A Good Financial Adviser Changes Everything
scenarios.text: A retired player introduces {J} to his financial adviser: honest, boring, brilliant. She reorganises everything: savings, pensions, a fund for his parents, a plan for retirement.

scenarios.title: {BRAND_fintech} Want {J} for Their Campaign
scenarios.text: {BRAND_fintech} want {J} as the face of a nationwide campaign: TV adverts, billboards, cashback with his face on it. {deal} for a year.

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: {J}'s face appears on every bus stop in Jakarta. His mother takes a photo with each one she passes.

ok.text: Two years, more money. {J}'s agent buys himself a new watch.

bad.text: The app signs a famous actor instead.

scenarios.title: Agent Says the Gulf Is Calling
scenarios.text: {J}'s agent calls, excited: a Gulf club is interested. Tax-free, triple his wage, a villa with a pool. “It would set your family up for generations.” But it would also mean a quieter league, far from the spotlight he's worked for.

choices.label: Yes, listen
choices.hint: Fans may call it a cash grab.
choices.text: {J} tells the agent to listen. The rumour leaks within a day.

choices.label: No, not yet
choices.text: “Not yet.” The agent sighs and says the offer won't last forever.

scenarios.title: Club Rewards {J}'s Form With a Raise
scenarios.text: The sporting director calls {J} in. No negotiation, no agent: the club is raising his wage in recognition of his form. “We look after people who look after us.”

scenarios.title: Hometown Mosque Needs Renovation
scenarios.text: The mosque where {J} learned to read the Quran as a boy is crumbling: a leaking roof, broken fans, a cracked floor. The imam calls to ask, very politely, if he might help.

choices.label: Fund it fully
choices.text: The renovation is finished before Ramadan. His father attends Friday prayers there and is congratulated by everyone.

choices.label: Contribute part
choices.text: {J} pays for the new roof. The imam mentions him in his sermon.

scenarios.title: Fake Agent Promises a European Trial
scenarios.text: A man on social media says he can get {J} a trial with a European club. All he needs is a fee for “registration and visa processing”. He has photos with famous players.

choices.label: Pay
choices.text: {J} pays {cost}. The man stops replying the next day. The photos were edited.

choices.label: Ask the club to check
choices.text: The club's lawyer recognises the name: a known scammer. {J} reports him to the federation.

scenarios.title: Limited-Edition Sneaker Drop
scenarios.text: A limited-edition sneaker drop, only five hundred pairs worldwide. A reseller has a pair in {J}'s size for {cost}.

choices.label: Buy them
choices.text: {J} keeps them in the box. He's afraid to wear them.

choices.label: Skip it
choices.text: {J} skips it. He checks resale prices for a week anyway.

scenarios.title: {J} Considers Starting a Foundation
scenarios.text: {J} wants to do something lasting: a foundation that pays for football boots and school fees for poor kids in his home region. Start-up cost: {cost}.

choices.label: Start it
choices.text: The {J} Foundation launches with fifty scholarships. The first photo of a girl in new boots makes him cry in the car park.

choices.label: Later
choices.text: {J} decides to wait until he retires.

scenarios.title: Foundation Scholar Makes an Academy
scenarios.text: A boy who received one of the foundation's first scholarships has been signed by a professional academy. He sends {J} a video of himself in his new training kit, saying thank you in a voice that hasn't broken yet.

scenarios.title: {J} Is Officially Rich
scenarios.text: The bank calls to offer “private client” services. A dedicated manager, a black card, an invitation to a members' club. Ten years ago, his family couldn't afford the bus to his trials.

choices.label: Stay grounded
choices.text: {J} declines the black card and keeps using the same bank app. He sends his first coach a new car.

choices.label: Enjoy it
choices.text: {J} upgrades everything: apartment, wardrobe, holidays. He deserves it. His living costs double.
